judged_text: Lark (and identically Office365CalendarService.ts:73 and BaseCalendarService) ignore the new credentialId/externalId arguments and always select `destinationCalendar[0]`, so when EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents loops over multiple collective destinations every non-Google credential inserts an event into the first host's calendar. For a collective booking with two non-Google destination calendars, credential B's createEvent call authenticates as host B but targets host A's calendar externalId, producing duplicate events on the wrong calendar (or a 404), while the same flow works for Google — an inconsistency introduced by only updating Google's service to consume credentialId.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Calendar.createEvent` to accept `(event, credentialId)` and updates GoogleCalendarService to select the destination calendar by matching `credentialId` (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`). However, LarkCalendarService and Office365CalendarService (and BaseCalendarService’s iCal path) were updated only to destructure `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then always use `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId`, i.e., `destinationCalendar[0]`, ignoring the per-credential selection. Meanwhile, EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now loops over multiple `event.destinationCalendar` entries for collective events and calls `createEvent` per credential/destination. For non-Google providers this will still target the first destination’s externalId even when authenticated as another credential, causing events to be inserted/updated in the wrong calendar (or fail).
